_comment: Field reference for every launcher tile. Read at every request.
HOST in a url is substituted at runtime with this node's MagicDNS name,
so the file stays tailnet-agnostic and survives a re-tailnet.
marker  - a path that exists only after that service is deployed. Drives
'installed' without touching the docker CLI (a systemd user unit
does not reliably inherit the docker group; status must not
depend on that).
setup   - path to setup.sh relative to the repo root. Never written in an
app.json: the generator fills in services/<dir>/setup.sh.
An `external` tile gives an absolute / ~-prefixed path for
code outside this repo; null means 'not built yet' -> planned.
env     - path to that service's gitignored .env. In an app.json it is
relative to the folder (".env"); external tiles use the setup rules.
never the values; revealing one is a separate POST. null means
the service has no .env at all.
author  - owner of the service's remote git repo (GitHub org/user, or
Codeberg for forgejo). Powers the 'c-wenlong' tab, which lists
the services whose code is the repo owner's own.
description - shown on the detail page. The shipped default: edits made
in the UI go to ~/services/launcher/overrides.json, never here.
control - start/stop/restart. THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for lifecycle
control on this box: app/web/server.py reads it from here and
services/ntfy-control/control_listener.py reads this same file off the
repo at runtime, so the phone and the web UI can never drift
into controlling different services or pausing different Kuma
monitors. Shape:
parts   - ordered list of {container|unit} to act on, in STOP
order; start is the exact reverse, so dependencies
come up first. Add "optional": true to a part that
may legitimately not exist (a compose profile that
is off) — its failure is logged and skipped.
primary - which part's state ntfy-control reports as the
service's state (the phone panel's up/down line).
Defaults to the first part; only needed when the
first thing stopped is not the user-facing one.
The launcher does not read it: its tile state
comes from its own health probe, not from a part.
kuma    - Uptime Kuma monitor paused on stop and resumed on
start, so deliberate downtime does not page the
phone. null when the service has no monitor.
A list of names when the service has several
monitors (adguard: ["adguard", "adguard-dns"]);
each is paused and resumed on its own.
stop_guard - optional argv run before Stop (launcher and
ntfy-control) and before Remove unless it is the
teardown.sh Remove runs anyway. In an app.json it
is relative to the service folder, first item a
file there (["teardown.sh", "--check-dns"]);
the generator makes it repo-relative. Non-zero
refuses the action before anything changes, with
its last stderr line as the reason. Restart is not
guarded: it is the usual fix for a stuck service.
locked  - present means NOT controllable, and the string is
the reason both UIs show and the API refuses with.
Absent control entirely also means not controllable. Three keys
are additionally hard-locked in server.py so that editing this
file cannot re-enable them: launcher, ntfy, ollama.
group    - bucket id from the file-level `groups` list. The launcher
paints a heading per bucket and sorts inside it. Unknown or
missing ids fall through to Other at the end.
order (in registry.json) is the order inside each bucket: daily drivers first.
File-level control plumbing: where the Kuma pause/resume helper lives.
Both paths go through the launcher's allowed-roots gate. The launcher
calls the EXISTING services/ntfy-control/kuma_toggle.py rather than talking to
Kuma itself, so there is one implementation of 'pause a monitor'.

external.name: manimkc
external.author: c-wenlong
external.description: Video-gen job server: POST a JSON brief and it renders a narrated ManimGL video, then uploads it to the Seafile `manimkc` library. A systemd user unit on 127.0.0.1:8090; the tile opens its /docs API page, since that is the whole UI. Code lives in its own repo at ~/dev/manimkc, not in this one, and narration runs through ElevenLabs, Sarvam or local Kokoro TTS.

external.name: ollama
external.author: ollama

control.locked: ollama is a system unit, so controlling it needs sudo — this endpoint deliberately has no sudo path

external.description: The local LLM runtime everything else talks to: Open WebUI chats through it and n8n workflows call it. Models pulled here are qwen3:8b, qwen3:4b and nomic-embed-text, and a loaded one claims roughly 5 GB of the box's 7.7 GB. No web UI of its own, so this tile reports status and never navigates. Known loose end: a systemd override binds it to *:11434, so it is LAN-reachable and not only tailnet-reachable.
